findings.source_quote: φυγοῦσα σὺν αὐτῷ, ἐν ἀλλοδαπῇ ὁρμήσασα
findings.english_quote: she fled with him, went abroad
findings.issue: “Went abroad” treats the foreign land as a destination, whereas ἐν ἀλλοδαπῇ identifies the location of the action expressed by ὁρμήσασα. On the lodging or anchoring sense of ὁρμέω, she stopped or stayed in a foreign land. Reading the form from ὁρμάω instead would concern setting out or moving there. The draft neither represents this distinction accurately nor discloses the lexical choice.
findings.suggested_revision: A source-transparent contextual proposal is “she fled with him, lodged in a foreign land,” followed by the remaining clauses unchanged. Add a note explaining the lodging/anchoring interpretation and preserving the alternative setting-out interpretation. Neither interpretation requires changing the supplied Greek; the revised wording requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: οὐκ ἐβουλήθην τὸ καθ’ ὑμᾶς αὐτῷ συναντιβαλεῖν, μέχρις ἂν ὑμῖν προσανάθωμαι.
findings.english_quote: I did not want to compare your circumstances with his account until I had consulted you.
findings.issue: The personal dative αὐτῷ identifies the old man as the participant in the proposed exchange. “With his account” substitutes an account for that person and leaves unrepresented Peter’s withholding of a discussion with him. The comparison or exchange expressed by συναντιβαλεῖν must retain this interpersonal element.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed wording: “I did not wish to bring up your circumstances with him until I had consulted you.” A note can explain that συναντιβαλεῖν suggests bringing accounts together for comparison in conversation. Review the replacement afresh before accepting it.

findings.source_quote: ἡμᾶς ἀγαπῶν ἀκριτὶ αὐτὸς μὲν ἐτελεύτησας
findings.english_quote: Loving us, you yourself died without judgment
findings.issue: The main text attaches ἀκριτὶ to dying. That is a defensible choice, but the note lists lexical alternatives without preserving the material alternative attachment to ἡμᾶς ἀγαπῶν: loving without discrimination or deliberation. “Without judgment” does not preserve that attachment once “Loving us” has been separated by a comma. The note also does not explain why the death attachment was preferred.
findings.suggested_revision: Expand the note to distinguish the two attachments explicitly. If retaining the present main text, explain why ἀκριτὶ is taken with ἐτελεύτησας and clarify that a hearing, tribunal, or unresolved legal proceeding is not asserted by the Greek. Preserve the alternative “loving us without discrimination/deliberation.” This disclosure issue does not make the construction untranslatable.

findings.source_quote: πλὴν μετ’. οὐ πολὺ ἡ μὲν μήτηρ
findings.english_quote: But after a little while my mother said
findings.issue: The English reads through the supplied period after μετ’, but the empty source_issues list does not disclose this conspicuous punctuation feature. The image-checked transcription verifies the printed reading; there is no basis here for calling it an OCR error or an unreadable source.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted source_issues note recording the supplied punctuation “μετ’. οὐ πολὺ” and explaining that the translation construes μετ’ with οὐ πολὺ despite the intervening period. Identify this as a disclosed print/editorial feature, not a restored lacuna. Any proposed deletion of the Greek period must be distinguished from the supplied reading; no source alteration is needed for the defensible English construction.
